sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 1:1
items.html: Light is everything that is received in the worlds in the manner of “existence from existence,” which includes everything except the substance of the vessels. See Item 2 and Item 24. (Part 1, Inner Observation, Item 18)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 2:1
items.html: The will to receive in the emanated being is called a vessel, and the abundance that it receives is called light. (Part 1, Inner Light, Item 6)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 3:1
items.html: Circular light is light that makes no discernment of degrees. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, Item 100)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 4:1
items.html: Simple light is light that includes the vessel within it, to the point that no discernment is made between the light and the vessel. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, Item 30)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 5:1
items.html: The light of Hochma is the light that is extended to the emanated being in the first expansion, which is the entirety of the vitality and the self of the emanated being. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, Item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 6:1
items.html: The light of Hassadim is a light that clothes the light of Hochma and is extended to the emanated being with the first overcoming. (Part 1, Inner Light, Chapter 1, Item 5)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 7:1
items.html: Empty air is the light of Hassadim before it clothes the light of Hochma. (Part 1, Inner Light, Chapter 1, Item 5)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 8:1
items.html: “Afterwards” means the consequence that comes by the force of the phase preceding it. See Item 20. (Part 1, Inner Observation, Item 34)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 9:1
items.html: See Item 39. (Part 1, Item 2)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 10:1
items.html: The upper light that expands from His self is one and simple like His self; and as it is in Ein Sof, so it is even in the world of Assiya, without any change or addition of form whatsoever. It is therefore called “one.” (Part 1, Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 1)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 11:1
items.html: The name “Creator” applies only to the innovation, that is, the invention of “existence from absence,” which is the substance of the vessels alone, defined as the “will to receive” in every essence, and which necessarily was not in His self before the creation. (Part 1, Inner Observation, Item 18)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 12:1
items.html: Adhesion is equivalence of form, which draws spiritual entities near and adheres them to one another, whereas disparity of form removes them from one another. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 30)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 13:1
items.html: If there is no recognition of any discernment whatsoever between the four degrees of the will to receive, they are said to be in a single evenness. (Part 1, Item 1)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 14:1
items.html: Light that comes out of the category of Emanator and comes into the discernment of an emanated being is called the “expansion” of the light. In truth the upper light is not affected by this in any way, like one who lights a candle from a candle, where the first lacks nothing; rather, it is named so after the reception of the emanated being. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 1)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 15:1
items.html: Phase one of the will to receive is discerned as the most refined of the three phases that follow it. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 90)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 16:1
items.html: Time is a certain sum of phases that cascade one from the other and are intertwined with one another in the order of cause and consequence, such as days, months, and years. (Part 1, Inner Observation, Item 34)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 17:1
items.html: Phase four of the will, which does not receive the upper light into herself because of the restriction, is discerned as the root of darkness. (Part 1, Inner Observation, Item 24)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 18:1
items.html: Hochma is the light of the self of the vitality of the emanated being. See Item 5. (Part 1, Inner Light, Chapter 1, Item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 19:1
items.html: Phase four of the will, which was emptied of light, is discerned as darkness in relation to the light; and in relation to the vessel she is discerned as “space,” for phase four herself was not withdrawn from the emanated being because of the restriction, but rather is present in it as an empty space without light. (Part 1, Item 1)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 20:1
items.html: When speaking of the relations of cause and consequence among the emanated beings, the cause is expressed by the word “before,” and the consequence of that cause is expressed by the word “afterwards.” See Item 16. (Part 1, Inner Observation, Item 34)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 21:1
items.html: “Singular” indicates the upper light, which shines and governs throughout the whole multiplicity of degrees that differ from one another, to the point of reversing them and equalising them to His singular form. “Unique” indicates the completion of that governance, that is, after He has already equalised them and returned their form to the discernment of singular like His own. See Item 10. (Part 1, Inner Observation, Item 1)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 22:1
items.html: Two different phases that have equalised their form to one another are found to be unified into a single phase. See Item 12. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 6)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 23:1
items.html: A lower degree sometimes rises to a level equal with the one above it, at a time when the upper one needs it for its own completion. The lower one is then discerned as the discernment of left, and the upper one as the discernment of right.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 24:1
items.html: The name “Former” applies to the imparting of the light to the worlds, which includes all of reality except the substance of the vessels. See above, Item 11 and Item 1. (Part 1, Inner Observation, Item 18)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 25:1
items.html: The will to receive in the emanated being is its vessel. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 6)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 26:1
items.html: The equalising of the form of the lower one to the upper one is an ascent “upward.” (Part 1, Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 27:1
items.html: Every cause is called an “Emanator” with respect to the degree that is its consequence. The name Emanator includes both the extension of the light and the vessel that receives the light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 28:1
items.html: The discernment of the will to receive that was imprinted in the souls is what separates them and “hews” them from the upper light, for disparity of form is what separates in spiritual entities (as above, Item 12). And the matter of the quarry of the soul is the discernment of the passage between the world of Atzilut and the world of Beria, which will be explained in its place. (Part 1, Inner Observation, Item 15)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 29:1
items.html: That which is of lesser importance than its fellow is discerned as being below its fellow. (Part 1, Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 30:1
items.html: See above, under the word “singular.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 31:1
items.html: Malchut of Ein Sof is the discernment of the will to receive that necessarily exists there. (Part 1, Inner Observation, Item 14)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 32:1
items.html: “From above downward” means from phase one to phase four, for phase four, which remained without light, is discerned as below all the degrees; and the fainter a thing’s will to receive, the more upper it is discerned to be, until phase one is discerned as being above them all. (Part 1, Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 33:1
items.html: It means that there is no discernment of deficiency there whatsoever, and it is inconceivable to add anything there to the completeness. (Part 1, Item 1)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 34:1
items.html: The more important is discerned as the discernment of “above,” and the inferior as the discernment of “below.” (Part 1, Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 35:1
items.html: The will to receive in the emanated being is the “place” for all the abundance and the light within it. (Part 1, Inner Observation, Item 11)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 36:1
items.html: A square is the degree that includes within it all four phases of the will. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Item 200)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 37:1
items.html: A triangle is a degree in which there are only the first three phases of the will. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 400)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 38:1
items.html: If the disparity of form of a degree from the root is not so evident as to separate it from the root, it is discerned as “touching” the root. The same applies between one degree and another. (Part 1, Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 5)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 39:1
items.html: Phase four in Ein Sof is called the “middle point,” after her oneness with the light of Ein Sof. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 40:1
items.html: The Sof [end] and conclusion of every emanated being is made by the detaining force in phase four, for the upper light ceases to shine there because she does not receive it. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 20)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 41:1
items.html: If there is no discernment of above and below among the four phases of the will to receive, it is discerned as a “circle” (that is, similar to a corporeal round shape, in which no discernment of above and below applies). For this reason the four phases are called four spherical circles, one inside the other, between which it is impossible to recognise or discern any discernments of above and below. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 100)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 42:1
items.html: “Upper” means the more important. (Part 1, Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 43:1
items.html: Two degrees between which there is no equivalence of form on any side are discerned as entirely separated from one another. (Part 1, Inner Observation, Item 12)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 44:1
items.html: Vacant is a place that is ready to receive corrections and completeness. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 4)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 45:1
items.html: It means that there is no discernment of degrees and sides in it. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 9)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 46:1
items.html: One who subdues his will, that is, one who detains himself and does not receive although he longs greatly to receive, is said to restrict himself. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 40)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 47:1
items.html: A line indicates that there is in it a discernment of above and below that was not there before it; it also indicates that its illumination is very scant compared with what preceded it. (Part 1, Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 1)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 48:1
items.html: The more a thing’s form is close and equal to its fellow’s, the nearer to it it is discerned to be. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 49:1
items.html: That part of the emanated being which is most equal to the form of the root is called Rosh [head]. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 4)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 50:1
items.html: The light of Hassadim is called Ruach. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 5)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 51:1
items.html: See Item 45.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 52:1
items.html: The holy names are explanations of how the lights alluded to in them come into attainment, in such a way that the name of a degree explains the ways of attainment in that degree. (Part 1, Inner Observation, Item 5)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 53:1
items.html: One who receives inside himself is discerned as having the light measured and bounded in the vessel; and one who receives outside himself is discerned as placing no boundary at all upon the light that he receives. (Part 1, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 54:1
items.html: Every renewal of form is discerned as spiritual motion, since it has become distinct from the previous form and has come out under a name of its own — similar to a part that separates from a corporeal thing, moves, and departs from its former place. (Part 1, Inner Observation, Item 33)
